note: Snapshot of a public sandbox PR with planted test cases. Verdicts are the recorded output of one live Promise Ledger run.

pr.title: Order history helpers
pr.body: **Test fixture PR #2 (deliberate, Promise Ledger G4).** Five review comments are posted on the first commit. A follow-up commit titled "Address all review comments" is then pushed. **Planted ground truth:** it truly fixes 2 (discount in orderTotal; rounding moved into formatPrice in another file), leaves 1 cosmetically touched but unfixed (empty-orders guard), partially fixes 1 (validates quantity but not price), and leaves 1 question unanswered (sort order).

items.author: priyansh-narang2308
items.body: **Blocking:** orderTotal ignores the cart's discount code. It should apply discountRate the same way total() does in cart.ts.

items.author: priyansh-narang2308
items.body: **Blocking:** This divides by zero when there are no orders. Guard the empty array and return 0.

items.author: priyansh-narang2308
items.body: **Question:** Why sort newest first here? The history screen shows oldest first.

items.author: priyansh-narang2308
items.body: **Suggestion:** Rounding belongs in formatPrice, not in the order logic. Move it there and return the raw total here.

items.author: priyansh-narang2308
items.body: **Blocking:** Validate that both quantity and unitPrice are positive before adding the line.

4316905916.rationale: The orderTotal function now calculates the subtotal and then subtracts the discount using discountRate, exactly as requested.

notes: No CI results on the latest commit
4316905924.rationale: The review comment requested guarding against division by zero when the orders array is empty, i.e., returning 0 for averageOrderValue when orders.length === 0. The latest code of src/orders.ts shows the function unchanged: it still computes `const sum = orders.reduce((n, o) => n + orderTotal(o), 0); return sum / orders.length;` with no check for empty array. No other modified files contain a fix for this function. Therefore the request remains unmet.
4316905924.whatIsMissing: A guard clause such as `if (orders.length === 0) return 0;` (or equivalent) at the start of averageOrderValue.

notes: The commented lines were not changed

4316905936.rationale: The reviewer asked why the sorting is newest‑first when the history screen shows oldest‑first. The code of `recentOrders` still sorts descending (newest first) and there is no reply or substantive change that answers the question.
4316905936.whatIsMissing: A reply explaining the sorting choice or a change to make the order oldest‑first.
